prompt: Write a short message to a new friend. Tell them your name, how old you are, where you live and what you like to do.

Write about your favourite food. What is it? When do you eat it? Who makes it?
Describe your bedroom. What is in it? What colour is it? Do you like it? Why?
Write about a normal day for you. What time do you get up? What do you do in the morning, afternoon and evening?

Write an email to a friend about a film you saw recently. What was it about? Who was in it? Would you recommend it?
An English-speaking friend is coming to your country for the first time. Write an email giving advice about what to see, what to eat and what to be careful about.
You have just finished a course (for example cooking, dancing or programming). Write an email to a friend describing the course, what you learned and whether you would recommend it.

Write a story that ends with this sentence: 'And that is why I will never travel without a map again.'
Write a story about a day when all the phones and computers in your city suddenly stopped working.
Is it better to study in the morning or in the evening? Give your opinion and one or two reasons.

You recently stayed at a hotel and left a personal item in your room. Write a letter to the hotel manager. In your letter: say when you stayed at the hotel; describe the item you left; explain what you would like the manager to do.

A friend has invited you to their wedding but you cannot attend. Write a letter to your friend. In your letter: thank them for the invitation; explain why you cannot attend; suggest another time you could meet.

You have seen an advertisement for a part-time job at a local museum. Write a letter to the museum manager. In your letter: explain which job you are interested in; describe your relevant experience; say when you are available for an interview.

There has been a lot of noise recently from a construction site near your home. Write a letter to your local council. In your letter: describe the problem; explain how it is affecting you; suggest what the council should do.

You are taking an evening course at a college but you are not satisfied with it. Write a letter to the course director. In your letter: give details of the course; explain what the problems are; say what you would like the college to do.

Your company is considering allowing employees to work from home two days a week. Your manager has asked for your opinion. Write a letter to your manager. In your letter: give your opinion on the proposal; explain the possible benefits and drawbacks; suggest how the arrangement could be organised.

Your town is planning to turn a public park into a shopping centre. Write a letter to the editor of a local newspaper. In your letter: explain why the park is important to the community; describe the likely effects of the plan; propose an alternative.

Professor: This week we are talking about learning habits. Some students prefer to study alone, while others prefer to study in groups. Which do you think is more effective, and why?

Anna: I study better alone. In a group, people talk about other things and I lose a lot of time.

Marco: Groups help me a lot. When I explain something to other people, I understand it better myself.

Professor: Many universities now record lectures and put them online. Some people think this is excellent because students can watch lectures again whenever they want. Others worry that students will stop coming to class. What is your opinion? Should universities record all lectures?

Kelly: I think recording lectures is a great idea. Sometimes I miss details, and being able to rewatch helps me prepare for exams.

Andrew: I disagree. If everything is online, students will procrastinate and the classroom discussion, which is the most valuable part, will disappear.

Professor: Cities around the world are trying to reduce car traffic. One proposal is to make public transport completely free. Do you think free public transport is a good policy for reducing traffic? Why or why not?

Yuki: Yes. If buses and trains are free, many people will leave their cars at home, and the air will be cleaner.

Daniel: I'm not sure. People use cars because they are convenient, not because buses are expensive. The money would be better spent on improving the service.

Professor: Some economists argue that a four-day working week would increase productivity and wellbeing without reducing output. Others believe it would be impractical for many industries. Do you think governments should encourage a four-day working week? Explain your view.

Priya: Trials in several countries showed employees were happier and just as productive. Governments should support this through tax incentives.

Leon: That works for office jobs, but hospitals, shops and factories cannot simply close for a day. A national policy would create more problems than it solves.

Professor: Artificial intelligence tools can now write essays, create images and compose music. Some people think these tools will make human creativity more valuable; others believe they will reduce it. What do you think, and why?

Sofia: I think AI will push people to be more original, because anything generic can now be produced by a machine.

Tom: I worry that young people will rely on these tools and never develop their own creative skills.

You recently joined a university photography club, but the meeting times have changed and you can no longer attend.

Write an email to the club organiser, Ms. Lee. In your email, do the following:

- Describe the problem with the new meeting times.
- Suggest a solution.
